meta.name: Asia & Middle East
meta.description: All Asian and Middle Eastern STEM & Physics universities, megascience labs, semiconductor & deep-tech hubs, and regional milestones.

eras.label: Pre-Classical & Ancient Foundations
eras.summary: Quantitative astronomy, metrology, optics, statics, hydrostatics, and naturalistic cosmology across Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and the Mediterranean.

eras.label: Golden Ages & Medieval Optics
eras.summary: Experimental optics, magnetism, algebra of motion, and precision observatories across the Islamic Golden Age, Song China, India, and medieval Europe.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution
eras.summary: Heliocentrism, telescopic astronomy, laws of planetary motion, universal gravitation, calculus, and analytical mechanics.

eras.label: Electromagnetism & Thermodynamics
eras.summary: Unification of electricity, magnetism, and light; statistical entropy; X-rays; and the discovery of radioactivity.

eras.label: Relativity & Quantum Century
eras.summary: Spacetime curvature, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, QED, semiconductor electronics, cosmic microwave background, and the Standard Model.

eras.label: Precision & Mega-Experiments
eras.summary: High-Tc superconductors, Bose-Einstein condensates, neutrino mass, dark energy, graphene, Higgs boson, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, and fusion ignition.

eras.label: Upcoming Frontier (2027–2045+)
eras.summary: Next-generation compact and burning-plasma fusion, 39 m optical telescopes, gigaton neutrino observatories, space interferometers, and post-LHC colliders.

events.title: Old Babylonian Mathematical Astronomy, Venus Tablet & Plimpton 322
events.summary: Compiled systematic 21-year synodic observations of Venus (Tablet of Ammisaduqa) alongside base-60 exact Pythagorean-triple tables (Plimpton 322), establishing predictive mathematical astronomy and sexagesimal angular measurement.
events.impact: Created the 360-degree circle, 60-minute hour, and quantitative planetary period tracking inherited by Greek and later astronomy.

events.title: Vedanga Jyotisha & Sulba Sutras: Calendar Astronomy & Geometry
events.summary: Formulated quantitative luni-solar timekeeping rules tracking solstices and lunar mansions (Vedanga Jyotisha) alongside explicit geometric statements of the Pythagorean relation and √2 approximations (Sulba Sutras).
events.impact: Established South Asia's continuous mathematical astronomy and computational geometry tradition.

events.title: Anaximander's Free-Floating Earth & Naturalistic Cosmology
events.summary: Anaximander proposed that Earth hangs unsupported in space by symmetry rather than resting on pillars or water, explaining rain, wind, and celestial motion through natural law.
events.impact: Pioneered naturalistic cosmology in the Mediterranean world, explaining cosmic equilibrium through symmetry rather than myth.

events.title: Mozi & the Mohist Canon: Camera Obscura, Optics & Inertia
events.summary: In the Mo Jing (Mohist Canon), described rectilinear propagation of light, inverted pinhole images (camera obscura), focal properties of concave and convex mirrors, and the persistence of motion absent opposing forces.
events.impact: Recorded the earliest known systematic treatise on geometrical optics and pinhole image formation.

events.title: Aryabhatiya: Earth's Rotation & Eclipse Mechanics
events.summary: In the Aryabhatiya, Aryabhata explained the apparent westward motion of the stars via Earth's axial rotation and gave a quantitative shadow-based model of solar and lunar eclipses.
events.impact: Laid mathematical and astronomical foundations for Indian and Islamic planetary science.

events.title: Brahmasphutasiddhanta: Arithmetic of Zero & Gravitational Attraction
events.summary: Formalized rules for zero and negative numbers while describing Earth's innate property of attracting all bodies toward itself (gurutvakarshan).
events.impact: Provided essential mathematical notation and planetary computation methods transmitted to Baghdad and Europe.

events.title: Al-Khwarizmi's Al-Jabr & Algorithmic Arithmetic
events.summary: Authored 'The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing' (al-jabr), establishing algebra as an independent discipline, alongside treatises popularizing Hindu-Arabic decimal numerals.
events.impact: Gave the world the words 'algebra' (from al-jabr) and 'algorithm' (from his Latinized name Algorismi).

events.title: Dream Pool Essays: Magnetic Declination & Focal Optics
events.summary: Described the magnetic needle compass, discovered true magnetic declination relative to geographic north, and analyzed focal points of concave mirrors and pinhole image inversion.
events.impact: Recorded the earliest known quantitative observations of geomagnetism and practical compass navigation.

events.title: Siddhanta Shiromani: Instantaneous Motion & Planetary Speeds
events.summary: Introduced tatkalika gati (instantaneous velocity) to compute planetary positions and stated that a vanishing derivative occurs at extrema, anticipating differential calculus.
events.impact: Advanced mathematical kinematics and spherical astronomy centuries before European calculus.

events.title: Maragheh Observatory & the Tusi Couple
events.summary: Founded a state-funded international research observatory equipped with giant mural quadrants and developed the Tusi couple, generating linear motion from two uniform circular motions.
events.impact: Produced the Ilkhanic Tables and planetary geometric mechanisms later echoed in Copernican astronomy.

events.title: Ulugh Beg Observatory & Zij-i-Sultani Star Catalogue
events.summary: Constructed a monumental 40-meter subterranean marble Fakhri sextant measuring Earth's axial tilt (23°30'17") and the sidereal year to within one minute of modern values.
events.impact: Compiled the most accurate naked-eye star catalogue of the pre-telescopic era (992 stars).

events.title: Neutrino Oscillations & Proof That Neutrinos Have Mass
events.summary: Super-Kamiokande demonstrated that atmospheric muon neutrinos change flavor in flight, followed by SNO resolving the solar neutrino problem—proving neutrinos carry non-zero mass.
events.impact: Delivered the first concrete laboratory physics beyond the original Standard Model.

events.title: Shinya Yamanaka Discovers Induced Pluripotent Stem (iPS) Cells
events.summary: Demonstrated that introducing just four transcription factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) reprograms mature adult skin cells back into embryonic-like pluripotent stem cells.
events.impact: Revolutionized regenerative medicine, personalized disease modeling, and 3D human organoids (2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine).

events.title: DeepMind's AlphaGo Defeats Go World Champion Lee Sedol
events.figure: David Silver, Demis Hassabis & Google DeepMind Team
events.summary: Combined deep policy/value neural networks with Monte Carlo Tree Search and self-play reinforcement learning to defeat 18-time world champion Lee Sedol 4–1—playing the iconic creative 'Move 37'.
events.impact: Demonstrated superhuman intuitive strategic reasoning a decade ahead of expectations and established the search + RL paradigm behind modern reasoning AI.

events.title: Hyper-Kamiokande Operations Begin
events.summary: A 260,000-ton ultrapure water Cherenkov detector—over 5× Super-Kamiokande's volume—entering photosensor installation in 2027 and scientific operations in 2028 to measure leptonic CP violation, supernova neutrinos, and proton decay.
events.impact: Probes why matter triumphed over antimatter in the early universe and tests Grand Unified Theories.

missions.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Vikram & Pragyan)
missions.summary: First mission to achieve a soft landing near the lunar south pole, performing in-situ thermophysical, plasma, seismic, and laser-breakdown elemental physics experiments.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measured the first steep subsurface thermal gradient in southern high-latitude regolith, detected sparse lunar near-surface ionosphere plasma, and confirmed sulfur via LIBS.

missions.name: Chang'e-4 & Yutu-2
missions.body: The Moon (Far Side — Von Kármán Crater)
missions.summary: First soft landing on the radio-quiet far side of the Moon, relayed via the Queqiao Earth–Moon L2 satellite to conduct low-frequency radio astronomy and deep regolith radar sounding.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Performed ultra-long-wavelength radio observations shielded from terrestrial RFI, measured lunar surface neutral-atom radiation doses, and profiled 40 m of subsurface ejecta stratigraphy.

missions.name: Hayabusa2
missions.summary: Returned 5.4 grams of pristine carbonaceous asteroid regolith from Ryugu to Earth in 2020 after firing an explosive copper impactor to excavate subsurface material; now cruising toward asteroid 1998 KY26.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Revealed low-cohesion rubble-pile impact mechanics in microgravity and delivered amino-acid-rich primitive solar-nebula samples unaltered by terrestrial atmosphere.

trails.title: From Laser-Vaporized Tin to Frontier AI
trails.tagline: How extreme ultraviolet plasma physics in Europe carves atomic-scale chips in Taiwan that power modern reasoning AI.

stops.title: ASML (EUV Lithography)
stops.bridge: Firing CO2 lasers 50,000 times per second at falling tin droplets creates 13.5 nm ultraviolet light—tested first inside imec's High-NA cleanrooms.

stops.title: imec Leuven (Sub-Nanometer R&D)
stops.bridge: imec defines the pre-competitive sub-2 nm nanosheet and CFET transistor blueprints that foundry giant TSMC scales to billions of chips.

stops.title: TSMC Global R&D Center
stops.bridge: TSMC etches 100-billion-transistor silicon dies and stitches them via CoWoS 3D packaging to manufacture NVIDIA's flagship AI GPUs.

stops.title: NVIDIA Research
stops.bridge: Massive coherent clusters of NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs supply the petaflops of matrix multiplication that train OpenAI's frontier models.

stops.title: OpenAI
stops.bridge: Scaling transformer pre-training and test-time reasoning raised urgent questions about how neural networks think—spurring former researchers to found Anthropic.

stops.title: Anthropic (Mechanistic Interpretability)
stops.bridge: Closes the loop by peering back inside silicon-hosted transformers with sparse autoencoders to map the hidden circuits of machine cognition.

trails.title: High Arctic & Svalbard Off-Grid Frontier
trails.tagline: Journey across Svalbard's seed vault, polar-orbit radomes, auroral radars, Greenland's 3.2 km ice-sheet apex, and drifting Arctic Ocean stations.

stops.title: Svalbard Global Seed Vault (78.2°N)
stops.bridge: Carved 120 m deep inside Spitsbergen permafrost, the Seed Vault safeguards over 1.3 million global food-crop varieties at -18°C even if external power fails.

stops.title: Svalbard Satellite Station (SvalSat)
stops.bridge: Just up Platåberget mountain, 100+ polar radomes catch every single orbit of NASA, ESA, and NOAA Earth-observing satellites.

stops.title: EISCAT Svalbard Radar (ESR)
stops.bridge: Perched inside the geomagnetic polar cusp, EISCAT's incoherent scatter dishes probe how solar wind pours directly into Earth's upper atmosphere.

stops.title: Ny-Ålesund & Zeppelin Observatory (78.9°N)
stops.bridge: The world's northernmost permanent civilian research village unites 10+ nations measuring pristine Arctic greenhouse gases, aerosols, and VLBI continental drift.

stops.title: Villum Research Station (81.6°N, Greenland)
stops.bridge: Cross the Greenland Sea to one of Earth's most remote off-grid atmospheric outposts tracking polar ozone chemistry and multi-year sea-ice loss.

stops.title: Alert Atmospheric Observatory (82.5°N)
stops.bridge: Just 817 km from the Geographic North Pole on Ellesmere Island, Alert records Earth's cleanest continuous high-Arctic CO₂ and methane baseline.

stops.title: Summit Station (Greenland Ice Sheet Apex)
stops.bridge: Climb to 3,216 m atop the Greenland Ice Sheet where GISP2 ice cores unlocked abrupt climate tipping points and millimeter telescopes scan the cosmos.

stops.title: Tara Polar Station (New Arctic Drift Lab)
stops.bridge: Finish aboard the next-generation ice-locked drifting polar lab engineered to freeze into the Central Arctic pack ice for 20 years of continuous oceanography.
